title: Book Three · Chapter 123: Seventeen in the Spring
story:
Saturday is Ronan's seventeenth birthday.

At ten, he takes his football onto the park field. Kai and the other boys are already there.

“Our oldest player,” Kai says.

“Our loudest player,” his friend adds.

Ronan lifts the ball. “Shall I give a speech?”

They pull him toward the grass before he can start.

The first game is close. Ronan sends one pass too far and has to run after it.

When he comes back, Kai points to a space near the side.

Ronan starts to argue. He wanted the next pass in the middle.

Kai has already turned toward the other player. Ronan looks at the space again. From there, he can see both of his teammates.

He moves out and lifts a hand.

The first ball does not reach him. He runs back to help, then tries the side again.

“Run, old man!” the other boy calls.

“I am running!”

Ronan stops the next pass with his foot. A player comes toward him, so he sends the ball back instead of trying to run through.

Kai moves past them. Ronan follows for a few steps, then leaves room near the side.

Nobody calls him old now. They are watching the ball. He feels his breath grow loud and keeps moving. When his friend calls, he is ready to look up. Later, he sees Kai near the side and puts the ball just ahead of his foot.

Kai scores. They finish two goals to one.

Ronan bends over with his hands on his knees. He is still smiling when Anna arrives with Lin.

“Too old?” she asks.

“Only for the next five minutes.”

They sit near the path while the other boys start another game. Lin stays to watch. Anna gives Ronan a small warm bun from a paper bag.

“Happy birthday.”

He thanks her and breaks it in two.

“I had breakfast,” she says.

“Then a small half.”

She takes it. They eat slowly while the ball moves across the field.

Afterward, Anna walks with him to the trees. She asks about the old man's voice, and he tries the first line again.

“I liked your voice yesterday,” she says.

“Old?”

“Yours.”

He looks at her. For once, he has no quick answer.

She takes his hand. He moves a little closer.

“Can I kiss you?”

“Yes.”

The kiss is brief. When he draws back, she is smiling.

“Very quiet,” she says.

He laughs softly. Then Kai calls his name across the grass, and they turn toward the field together.

That evening, Mum cooks fish for the birthday meal. Dad comes home after work and washes before he sits down.

Ronan tells them about the match. He leaves out the old voice this time. Dad has heard it three times already.

Mum gives Ronan a large piece of fish.

“Seventeen.”

“Does the plate grow every year?” he asks.

“Only if you wash it,” Dad says.

After the meal, Ronan carries the plates to the kitchen. Dad brings the bowls. Mum sits near the open door with her tea.

The spring evening is still light. Ronan dries his hands and finds his football beside the bike.

He calls to Dad, who turns from the kitchen step. Ronan rolls the ball gently across the yard. Dad stops it with one work shoe, looks toward Mum, and sends it back.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

score＝进球、得分；speech＝讲话；brief＝短暂的；draw back＝向后退开一点。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan在哪天满十七岁？球场上他做出了什么有用的配合？
2. Anna怎样表达亲近？晚上一家人怎样一起过这个生日？

## 读句子

**The kiss is brief.**

拆开看：The kiss / is / brief.

这个吻／是／短暂的。
